newsitem.title: USA: FOOTBALL-FLORIDA TO MEET TOP-RANKED FLORIDA ST IN SUGAR BOWL.
newsitem.headline: FOOTBALL-FLORIDA TO MEET TOP-RANKED FLORIDA ST IN SUGAR BOWL.

text.p: Top-ranked Florida State and third-ranked Florida will meet for at least a share of college football's national championship January 2 at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans, the bowl alliance announced on Sunday.
Sixth-ranked Nebraska (10-2), which was headed for the Sugar Bowl until Saturday's upset by Texas, will meet Virginia Tech (10-1) in the Orange Bowl on New Year's Eve in Miami.
Seventh-ranked Penn State (9-2) will face Texas (8-4) in the Fiesta Bowl on New Year's Day in Tempe, Arizona.

Florida State upset then top-ranked Florida 24-21 two weeks ago to complete an 11-0 regular season. The only other school with a spotless record is second-ranked Arizona State (11-0), which faces fourth-ranked Ohio State (10-1) in the Rose Bowl for a shot at the national title.

Representatives of the three games in the bowl alliance -- the Sugar, Fiesta and Orange Bowls -- shunned fifth-ranked Brigham Young (13-1), instead selecting national powers with television drawing power, despite lesser records.

"BYU is a fine team with a fine tradition," said John Junker, executive director of the Fiesta Bowl. "But we thought Penn State was the logical choice because it brought the most pluses to the table."

After upending Florida, Florida State began gearing up for a Sugar Bowl showdown with defending national champions Nebraska, which was a prohibitive favourite in Saturday's Big 12 title game. But Texas stunned Nebraska 37-27, altering the Bowl game picture.
"I didn't think we'd be back in the Sugar Bowl," admitted Florida coach Steve Spurrier.
"I spent all day Friday and Saturday preparing for Nebraska," said Florida State coach Bobby Bowden, whose Seminoles are looking for a second national title in four years.
